data.why: The repo's own sample_compounds.csv only has compound names, which require a live PubChem lookup the sandboxed server cannot make, so a SMILES-column batch file is provided to exercise descriptor/drug-likeness/MRM calculation without network access.

goals: Look up a known drug by name or CAS number and review its computed physicochemical properties
Paste a SMILES string directly to get descriptors, drug-likeness flags, functional groups and MRM transitions without needing a name lookup
Batch-upload a CSV/Excel of compounds (by SMILES column) and review the combined properties table
Evaluate a compound against Lipinski/Veber/Ghose/Egan drug-likeness rules to judge oral bioavailability
Generate suggested MRM precursor/product ion transitions for mass spec method design
Export the computed property and MRM tables and download the structure image

review.summary: This is an accurate, well-evidenced tree of the offline path: SMILES and batch input, then descriptors, drug-likeness, MRM transitions and export, with faithful labels; a second agent replayed every task and feature, and every screen I opened matches its node. Before filing, it needs the README's primary name/CAS lookup and the PubChem material added as blocked branches, the fullscreen and invalid-input nodes merged into their parent tasks, and the feature list fixed by adding a functional-group detector and splitting the oversized f1.
